entries.proposition: The review's thesis: BBB dysfunction is both cause and consequence of seizures, an 'important link' in epilepsy pathophysiology.
entries.snippet: Such BBB dysfunction can both trigger and sustain seizures, thus being a cause and a consequence of epileptic activity, which makes the BBB an important link in the pathophysiology of epilepsy [5].

experimental_context.system: narrative review of blood-brain barrier disruption in epilepsy (human MRI/tissue/CSF studies, rodent status epilepticus, TBI and ischaemia models)

entries.proposition: Human evidence: seizure-related BBB opening on imaging, persistent interictal leakage in drug-resistant epilepsy, and reduced leakage after successful focus resection.
entries.snippet: At the same time, BBB leakage in patients with drug-resistant epilepsy is persistent and observed inter-ictally [30,31].

experimental_context.system: narrative review of blood-brain barrier disruption in epilepsy (human MRI/tissue/CSF studies, rodent status epilepticus, TBI and ischaemia models)

entries.proposition: Evidence on endothelial tight-junction protein in human tissue is mixed: claudin-5 reduced in resected temporal lobe in one report, increased in microvasculature in another.
entries.snippet: However, the study of the expression of tight junction proteins specifically in endothelial cells in the microvasculature of TLE patients showed an increase in claudin-5 expression and a decrease in occludin expression [59].

experimental_context.system: narrative review of blood-brain barrier disruption in epilepsy (human MRI/tissue/CSF studies, rodent status epilepticus, TBI and ischaemia models)

entries.proposition: Albumin in tissue: post-mortem and resected tissue from epilepsy patients shows extravasated serum albumin and activated astrocytes.
entries.snippet: Post-mortem immunohistochemical investigation of the hippocampus of epilepsy patients showed the presence of extravasated serum albumin and activated astrocytes [190]
entries.anchor: 5.2 Extravasation of albumin and TGF-beta signaling

experimental_context.system: narrative review of blood-brain barrier disruption in epilepsy (human MRI/tissue/CSF studies, rodent status epilepticus, TBI and ischaemia models)

entries.proposition: Rodent albumin experiments: intracerebral albumin increased susceptibility to kainic acid seizures and lowered the hippocampal after-discharge threshold; albumin binds astrocytic TGF-beta type II receptors; blocking the receptor prevents albumin-induced epileptiform activity.
entries.snippet: Intracerebral administration of albumin increased susceptibility to KA-induced seizures during the acute period after albumin injection and reduced the after-discharge threshold in the hippocampus in the long-term period after albumin injection
entries.anchor: 5.2 Extravasation of albumin and TGF-beta signaling

experimental_context.system: narrative review of blood-brain barrier disruption in epilepsy (human MRI/tissue/CSF studies, rodent status epilepticus, TBI and ischaemia models)

entries.proposition: The albumin pathway proceeds through astrocytic TGF-beta receptor II and reduces Kir4.1, with extracellular potassium and glutamate accumulation.
entries.snippet: Activation of TGF-β signaling leads to downregulation of Kir4.1 and accumulation of extracellular K+ and glutamate and a subsequent increase in neuronal excitability [199].

experimental_context.system: narrative review of blood-brain barrier disruption in epilepsy (human MRI/tissue/CSF studies, rodent status epilepticus, TBI and ischaemia models)

entries.proposition: Clinical support for the TGF-beta arm is raised CSF TGF-beta1 and upregulated pathway components in resected temporal lobe tissue.
entries.snippet: Increased concentration of TGF-β1 has been found in the CSF of patients with drug-resistant epilepsy [207], and TGFβRIs are upregulated in the temporal lobe of such patients [208].

experimental_context.system: narrative review of blood-brain barrier disruption in epilepsy (human MRI/tissue/CSF studies, rodent status epilepticus, TBI and ischaemia models)

entries.proposition: Plasminogen activation: tPA-null mice show less seizure susceptibility and BBB leakage, neuroserpin-null mice severe seizures and early barrier loss (rodent, kainic acid).
entries.snippet: In studies on knockout mice, tPA-deficient tPA−/− mice have demonstrated decreased susceptibility to seizures [161,162], while neuroserpin-deficient Nsp−/− mice, on the contrary, have developed very severe seizures in response to KA injection [161].

experimental_context.system: narrative review of blood-brain barrier disruption in epilepsy (human MRI/tissue/CSF studies, rodent status epilepticus, TBI and ischaemia models)

entries.proposition: Immune cells: monocyte and neutrophil infiltration contributes to damage in kainic acid and pilocarpine models, but infiltration of leukocytes may be protective in some contexts.
entries.snippet: At the same time, some processes accompanying BBB disruption may be a compensatory response to brain damage; for example, infiltration of peripheral leukocytes can have a protective effect via recruitment of B-cells to the brain
entries.anchor: 8. BBB targeting as a therapeutic strategy

experimental_context.system: narrative review of blood-brain barrier disruption in epilepsy (human MRI/tissue/CSF studies, rodent status epilepticus, TBI and ischaemia models)

entries.proposition: Drug-resistance paradox: despite increased permeability of the damaged barrier, dysfunction is said to decrease drug penetration; the transporter hypothesis remains debated.
entries.snippet: Despite the increased permeability of the damaged BBB, its dysfunction leads to a decrease in drug penetration to the brain in epilepsy patients [9].
entries.anchor: 7. BBB dysfunction and resistance to antiepileptic drugs

experimental_context.system: narrative review of blood-brain barrier disruption in epilepsy (human MRI/tissue/CSF studies, rodent status epilepticus, TBI and ischaemia models)

entries.proposition: Therapeutic candidates (losartan, microRNA antagonists, levetiracetam, valproate, imatinib) rest on rodent models; the review says none has fully prevented epileptogenesis and most approaches are far from the clinic.
entries.snippet: However, so far, none of the studied candidates have exhibited an ability to fully prevent epileptogenesis.

experimental_context.system: narrative review of blood-brain barrier disruption in epilepsy (human MRI/tissue/CSF studies, rodent status epilepticus, TBI and ischaemia models)

entries.proposition: An observational cohort of hypertensive patients on angiotensin receptor blockers (losartan in particular) is cited as showing lower new-onset epilepsy.
entries.snippet: Interestingly, a cohort study on patients with arterial hypertension has shown that patients receiving angiotensin receptor blockers, particularly losartan, demonstrated a lower incidence of new-onset epilepsy compared to patients receiving other groups of antihypertensive medications [269].

experimental_context.system: narrative review of blood-brain barrier disruption in epilepsy (human MRI/tissue/CSF studies, rodent status epilepticus, TBI and ischaemia models)

entries.proposition: The conclusion says the timing and response of components differ by insult and that future work must define spatiotemporal detail.
entries.snippet: Therefore, future research is needed to elucidate the precise spatiotemporal details of BBB damage and NVU dysfunction across different epileptogenic contexts.
